ethiopia.title: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers 12 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Peter Kamasa Tuesday, October 13 Olympic Qualifiers (Second Leg) Ethiopia vs Rwanda (Dire Dawa Stadium, Ethiopia) Rwanda women's national team captain Angeline Ndakimana is confident that Amavubi can overturn their first-leg deficit and eliminate Ethiopia when the two sides meet in the return leg of the 2028 CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers at Dire Dawa Stadium on Tuesday. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Rwanda head into the decisive encounter trailing 1-0 on aggregate following a heartbreaking defeat in the first leg in Kigali on October 7. Despite the setback, Ndakimana believes Amavubi have the quality and determination to respond away from home and keep their Olympic qualification hopes alive. "We made a mistake in the first leg, but we can turn things around away from home. They are a good team, but we can beat them," Ndakimana said. "We have been preparing well for this match because we know how difficult it is going to be. Everyone in the team is focused on achieving a positive result," she added. Head coach André Casa Mbungo shares his captain's optimism, insisting that the team has worked to address the shortcomings that cost them in the first leg. "We corrected our mistakes and we want to make sure that we get a good result. I know it is hard, but it is possible," Casa Mbungo said. The first leg appeared destined to end in a goalless draw before a stoppage-time own goal by Rwanda defender Lydia Uzayisenga handed Ethiopia a crucial advantage. Uzayisenga inadvertently turned Abebe Mihiret's cross into her own net in the second minute of added time, leaving Rwanda with a difficult task ahead of the return fixture. With their Olympic dream on the line, Amavubi must produce a strong performance in Ethiopia to keep their qualification campaign alive. Rwanda need to win by at least two goals to overturn the deficit and secure progression to the third round. The winner of the tie will advance to the next stage, where either Tanzania or Botswana awaits as the qualification campaign continues. Read the original article on New Times . ethiopia.title: Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers
ethiopia.content: Rwanda/Ethiopia: Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Rwanda/Ethiopia: Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers 14 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Peter Kamasa Rwanda's hopes of qualifying for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games came to an end on Tuesday after the Amavubi held Ethiopia to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their CAF Women's Olympic qualifiers in Dire Dawa, losing 2-1 on aggregate. Needing a victory to overturn a 1-0 first-leg deficit, Rwanda travelled to Ethiopia knowing that anything less than a win would end their Olympic dream. However, the hosts struck first, leaving the visitors with an even tougher task. Ethiopia took the lead in the 28th minute through Mesay Temesgen, extending their aggregate advantage to 2-0 and putting Rwanda under pressure to respond. The goal forced André Casa Mbungo's side to push forward in search of a lifeline, but their efforts went unrewarded before the break. Emerance Niyonshuti came close to equalising in first-half stoppage time but failed to convert a one-on-one opportunity. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Trailing 2-0 on aggregate at half-time, Rwanda returned for the second half with renewed determination, taking the initiative and putting the Ethiopian defence under sustained pressure. Evelyne Ishimwe Mizero nearly reduced the deficit in the 60th minute but narrowly missed the target following a corner-kick situation. With time running out, Mbungo made tactical changes in an attempt to revive his team's hopes, introducing Josiane Uwihirwe for Régine Ihirwe in the 67th minute. The substitutions helped Rwanda maintain their attacking momentum, but Ethiopia remained resilient as they sought to protect their aggregate lead. The Amavubi continued to push forward, refusing to give up despite the mounting pressure and the diminishing time available to force a comeback. Their persistence finally paid off in the 89th minute when Ishimwe Mizero found the back of the net to make it 1-1 on the night, briefly raising hopes of a dramatic turnaround. However, the late equaliser came too late to change the outcome of the tie. Ethiopia held on to secure a 2-1 aggregate victory and advance to the next qualifying round, bringing Rwanda's campaign to an end. Ultimately, the first-leg defeat proved decisive for the Amavubi, whose late fightback in Ethiopia was not enough to keep their Los Angeles 2028 Olympic ambitions alive. Ethiopia will now face either Tanzania or Botswana in the next round as they continue their quest to qualify for the Olympic Games. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia, Beginnings Fund Launch U.S.$90 Million Investment to End Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, Beginnings Fund Launch U.S.$90 Million Investment to End Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, Beginnings Fund Launch U.S.$90 Million Investment to End Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths 13 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — The Ministry of Health and the Beginnings Fund have launched a five-year, 90 million USD investment to accelerate Ethiopia's efforts to prevent maternal and newborn deaths and to strengthen health services. Health Minister Dr. Mekdes Daba stated at the launching ceremony that the partnership with a coalition of global philanthropic foundations, investors, and institutional partners marks a major milestone toward achieving this goal. "Our partnership with the Beginnings Fund assumes a particular significance because we are launching a landmark initiative of investment of 90 million USD dedicated to accelerating progress towards ending preventable maternal and newborn deaths in Ethiopia," she said. Dr. Mekdes added that the investment would help ensure that "the most competent professionals" are at the forefront of care, so that mothers can trust and utilize public health facilities. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn She noted that Ethiopia has recorded remarkable progress over two decades, with maternal mortality significantly reduced and more women seeking antenatal care. However, she stressed against complacency: "We cannot be satisfied with what we have improved in urban areas. This is a time for us to challenge ourselves and deliver for our community." Beginnings Fund CEO Alice Kang'ethe said the organization's role is to support government priorities rather than pursue separate agendas. "The fund is focused on supporting governments to accelerate progress... by investing in people, products, and health systems for quality maternal and newborn care," she stated. Kang'ethe expressed confidence that Ethiopia could surpass the Sustainable Development Goal targets on mortality reduction. "We know what it takes to address preventable deaths. Solutions exist, including new innovations. Our joint role is to ensure these interventions are delivered quickly, with quality, to all women and newborns, consistently and at scale," she said. UAE Ambassador to Ethiopia Abdalla Hassan Alshamsi praised Ethiopia's leadership and commitment to improving healthcare. "This achievement reflects Ethiopia's leadership and its dedication to improving healthcare for its people," he said. He added that the Gates Foundation initiative launched in Abu Dhabi aims to improve healthcare for 34 million mothers and newborns across Africa and help prevent more than 300 million avoidable deaths by 2031. The Beginnings Fund is backed by philanthropies including the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity, the Gates Foundation, the Children's Investment Fund Foundation, and Delta Philanthropies. It operates in Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Lesotho, Ghana, and Nigeria. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia, France Seek Stronger Economic Cooperation Amid Reform Efforts
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, France Seek Stronger Economic Cooperation Amid Reform Efforts - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, France Seek Stronger Economic Cooperation Amid Reform Efforts 13 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — An Ethiopian delegation led by Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), Eyob Tekalign held talks with Thomas Revial, Assistant Secretary at the French Treasury, on strengthening economic cooperation between the two countries on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. The discussions reviewed Ethiopia and France's longstanding economic partnership, with a focus on progress in Ethiopia's ongoing macroeconomic reforms and France's continued engagement in supporting the country's development priorities. The two sides also explored opportunities to expand cooperation in development financing, debt sustainability, investment, and institutional capacity building, underscoring the importance of a sustained partnership in strengthening economic stability and promoting sustainable growth. The meeting reaffirmed the value of continued dialogue and cooperation between Ethiopia and France in advancing economic reforms, mobilizing development finance, and creating opportunities for mutually beneficial growth, ENA learned. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia, IMF Explore Stronger Support for Fiscal and Monetary Reforms
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, IMF Explore Stronger Support for Fiscal and Monetary Reforms - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, IMF Explore Stronger Support for Fiscal and Monetary Reforms 13 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia's delegation has held separate bilateral meetings with the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) Fiscal Affairs Department and Monetary and Capital Markets Department (MCM) to strengthen institutional capacity and advance the country's ongoing economic reform agenda. The discussions took place on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. Talks with the IMF's Fiscal Affairs Department focused on building the capacity of Ethiopia's Ministry of Finance, reviewing ongoing technical assistance and identifying opportunities for additional support aligned with the Ministry's reform priorities. In a separate meeting with the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, the delegation discussed strengthening the institutional capacity of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), reviewing ongoing IMF technical assistance and exploring further support to advance the central bank's reform agenda. The engagements underscore Ethiopia's efforts to deepen cooperation with the IMF, enhance the capacity of key economic institutions and reinforce ongoing fiscal and monetary reforms, according to the Central Bank of Ethiopia. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia-Russia Agribusiness Ties Poised to Boost Technology Transfer, Food Security
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia-Russia Agribusiness Ties Poised to Boost Technology Transfer, Food Security - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia-Russia Agribusiness Ties Poised to Boost Technology Transfer, Food Security 13 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Strengthening agribusiness cooperation between Ethiopia and Russia could accelerate technology transfer, boost agricultural productivity, enhance food security, and unlock new investment opportunities, stakeholders said during a roundtable discussion hosted by ENA. Russian Trade Representative to Ethiopia Yaroslav Tarasyuk highlighted that Ethiopia has emerged as one of Russia's top 10 trading partners in Africa. Tarasyuk noted significant momentum in bilateral trade through 2025, driven by a fourfold increase in Russian exports to Ethiopia and a doubling of Ethiopian exports to Russia. Ethiopia exported 18,000 tons of green coffee valued at 123 million USD to Russia, alongside flowers, fruits, vegetables, avocados, herbs, and other agricultural products. Russia, meanwhile, supplies Ethiopia with key commodities, including mineral fertilizers and sunflower oil. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Tarasyuk stressed the need to expand cooperation beyond conventional trade to include joint investments, technology transfer, and local production of agricultural machinery and inputs. He affirmed that Russia is ready to share advanced agricultural technologies and support the development of Ethiopia's manufacturing capacity. He identified sunflower cultivation, poultry production, and dairy development as promising areas for bilateral cooperation, noting that expanding domestic sunflower production could help Ethiopia reduce its reliance on imported edible oils. Weyssa Garedew, Crop Commercialization Program Director at the Agricultural Transformation Institute, noted that agriculture remains a central pillar of Ethiopia's economy. The sector contributes approximately 30 to 40 percent of gross domestic product, supports the livelihoods of around 79 million people, and accounts for about 80 percent of exports. However, Garedew pointed out that population growth, climate change, and limited access to inputs continue to constrain productivity. He emphasized the critical need for reliable fertilizer supplies, mechanization, agrochemicals, and modern technologies to transform the sector. He added that stronger cooperation with Russia could facilitate technology transfer, build local capacity, and introduce solutions tailored to Ethiopia's agricultural conditions. Furthermore, plans are underway to establish approximately 50 agribusiness companies to accelerate commercialization, boost agro-processing, and improve market access for farmers. Meanwhile, Habtamu Million, Country Head of Promising International Trading Company, emphasized that expanding domestic processing of agricultural commodities is essential for improving food security, creating jobs, and facilitating technology transfer. He noted that Russia's expertise in grain production, storage, transportation, and processing could significantly strengthen Ethiopia's food-processing industry. His company is currently exploring opportunities in grain milling and edible-oil extraction to increase domestic supply and generate higher economic value. Habtamu also stressed the need to upgrade processing facilities, product quality, and packaging to make Ethiopian agricultural exports more competitive internationally. Dareskedar Taye, President of the Union of African Diasporas in Russia and Head of the Ethiopian Community Association, underscored the key role the diaspora plays in bridging Ethiopian and Russian businesses. He noted that Africans living in Russia can leverage their understanding of both markets to drive investment, technology transfer, and commercial partnerships. Dareskedar emphasized the need for improved investment conditions, streamlined administrative procedures, and stronger institutional links to maximize this potential. Tsedeke Abate, former Director General of the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research, stressed the urgency of prioritizing productivity, diversification, value addition, and research to meet the needs of Ethiopia's rapidly growing population. Tsedeke noted that Ethiopia spent approximately 2.6 billion USD on food imports in 2023 alone, including 684 million USD on cooking oil. Expanding domestic production and processing, he argued, is vital to reducing import dependency and raising export value. He further emphasized that international partnerships must be grounded in mutual equality, with Ethiopia and other African nations taking the lead in defining their own agricultural agendas. Stronger ties with Russia could bolster fertilizer supplies, advance agricultural research, and support training institutions. The stakeholders agreed that deepening Ethiopia-Russia agribusiness cooperation will increase agricultural productivity, expand domestic processing, improve food security, and open new avenues for investment and technology transfer. ethiopia.title: All of Africa Today - October 13, 2026
ethiopia.content: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 13, 2026 - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Africa: All of Africa Today - October 13, 2026 AllAfrica AllAfrica logo 13 October 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda WHO Launches Five-Year Strategy to Detect Health Threats Faster The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched a new five-year strategy to help every country detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. The strategy builds on the work of the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, established in 2021 after the COVID-19 pandemic exposed gaps. Since its creation, the Hub has worked with 160 WHO member states, 190 partner organisations and thousands of scientists and policymakers to strengthen global disease surveillance. The plan focuses on five key initiatives, including using artificial intelligence to identify potential health threats, strengthening genomic sequencing to track emerging pathogens and connecting experts in data science and disease modelling. It will also support countries in sharing health data securely and improving cooperation between human, animal and environmental health systems. WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the strategy provides a clear path towards a world where countries can respond to health threats before they develop into major crises. The organisation says sustained investment and international partnerships will be essential to achieving this goal. South Africa's Deputy Police Chief Resigns Amid Criminal Charges Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines South Africa's Deputy National Police Commissioner, Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya, has resigned from the police service three weeks after being charged with sexual offences. His lawyer submitted the resignation letter during a disciplinary hearing. Police spokesperson Athlenda Mathe said his departure would be treated as a dishonourable discharge because he was still facing disciplinary proceedings at the time of his resignation. Sibiya has been in custody since his arrest in September. Sibiya faces several serious allegations, including the sexual grooming of a 16-year-old girl, rape, human trafficking and links to organised crime figures. He denies the allegations of criminal links and sexual grooming. He admits having sex with an 18-year-old woman but maintains that it was consensual. Allegations against him also emerged during the Madlanga Commission, a public inquiry investigating claims of police corruption and collusion with criminal networks. He has been accused of interfering with investigations into political killings in KwaZulu-Natal and receiving cash and 20 impalas from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract. Sibiya has denied the allegations. Renewed Fighting in Tigray Raises Fears of Wider Regional War Renewed fighting in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region is raising fears of a wider conflict involving Eritrea and other neighbouring countries. Tensions escalated after reports that Eritrean forces crossed into Ethiopia, prompting Ethiopian forces to launch drone strikes against troops and equipment. Eritrea has denied reports of the incursion, while accusing Ethiopia of using the allegations as a pretext to pursue its ambitions for access to the Red Sea port of Assab. Local sources, however, reported clashes involving Eritrean forces at several locations in Tigray. The renewed violence follows the collapse of a fragile peace agreement that ended the 2020–2022 war. The conflict is unfolding amid shifting alliances between rival armed groups and growing tensions between Ethiopia and its neighbours. Tigray's ruling Tigray People's Liberation Front has vowed to continue fighting after federal forces and a pro-government militia captured the regional capital, Mekelle, on 3 October. The TPLF has also aligned with other opposition groups seeking to challenge Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Analysts warn that the conflict could develop into three possible scenarios: the proliferation of armed groups, a prolonged military stalemate, or a full-scale war between Ethiopia and Eritrea. The humanitarian consequences could be severe, particularly in Tigray, where about one million people remain displaced, and nearly four million need urgent assistance. Drought, food shortages, and difficulties delivering aid are adding to the crisis. Drought and Conflict Push Sudan Closer to Famine The risk of famine is growing in parts of Sudan as severe drought worsens the humanitarian crisis caused by ongoing conflict, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a global food security monitoring partnership supported by United Nations agencies. A new alert warns that malnutrition is worsening in several areas, particularly in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan. Aid organisations are struggling to reach affected communities because of insecurity, restricted access and a severe shortage of funding. In Eastern Jebel Marra, South Darfur, surveys in two displacement camps found acute malnutrition among children at 38% and 30.8%, both above the threshold associated with famine. More than half of Sudan has been affected by the drought, destroying crops and leaving families without enough food or income. In North Darfur, 64% of cropland is showing poor plant growth and late rains have not managed to save most cereal crops. Food prices are expected to continue to rise. There has also been mass displacement in Greater Kordofan, where since October 2025 more than 300,000 people have been forced to flee their homes. Attacks and insecurity are putting aid workers at risk, while many children are going without life-saving treatment for severe malnutrition. By 8 October, less than half of Sudan's humanitarian appeal had been funded. The IPC has called for an end to the fighting, safe access for aid agencies and a major increase in funding to prevent further loss of life. Lagos Court Clears Way for Inquest into Chimamanda Adichie's Son's Death The Lagos State High Court has cleared the way for a coroner's inquest into the death of Nkanu Esege, the son of renowned Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie. Justice Aishat Opesanwo dismissed an application by Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited, which operates Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital, seeking to stop the inquiry. The hospital argued that the cremation of Nkanu's body made a post-mortem examination impossible and deprived the coroner of the authority to proceed. Nkanu died on 7 January 2026 following medical procedures, prompting an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. In her ruling, Justice Opesanwo said the law requires an inquest when the circumstances of a death meet the conditions set out in the Coroners System Law of Lagos State 2007. She said that the absence of the body did not automatically prevent the inquiry from taking place or make it speculative. The judge also rejected the hospital's arguments concerning the handling of statements and evidence from medical personnel, saying the coroner has discretion over how the proceedings are conducted. She stressed that a coroner's inquest is a fact-finding exercise intended to establish who died, and how, when and where the death occurred. It is not a criminal trial to determine guilt or assign blame. The ruling allows the inquest to proceed. ethiopia.title: Egypt Exacerbating Sudan's Civil War With Recent Massacre of Over 200 Civilians
ethiopia.content: Sudan: Egypt Exacerbating Sudan's Civil War With Recent Massacre of Over 200 Civilians - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Sudan: Egypt Exacerbating Sudan's Civil War With Recent Massacre of Over 200 Civilians 12 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Egypt has reportedly massacred at least 200 Sudanese miners and wounded many others in targeting mining sites in Sudan's North Al-Wadi area. Many observers say the recent civilian attacks are part of Egypt's direct and indirect involvement in Sudan's ongoing conflict, aimed at maximizing its own interests. In a recent interview with ENA, Abdulshakur Abdulsamad, Senior Researcher at the Center for Strategic Studies and Regional Integration Initiative, underscored that Egypt seeks to prolong the war in Sudan to continue benefiting from the country's water resources. The ongoing conflict allows Egypt to benefit from larger-than-usual quantities of water that Sudan has been unable to utilize, the senior researcher noted. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines In this regard, Egypt reportedly carried out airstrikes on artisanal mining sites in the Shamal al-Wadi area of Sudan's northeastern Red Sea region on Saturday, October 10, as miners were preparing to begin work, according to Sudan Tribune . In response, the Civil Democratic Alliance of the Forces of the Revolution, known as Somoud, confirmed and condemned the airstrikes, which it said were carried out by the Egyptian military inside Sudanese territory. "Targeting civilians and endangering their lives is unacceptable and cannot be justified on any security grounds. We hold the leadership of the authorities appointed by the Sudanese Armed Forces responsible for what occurs in these areas under their control," Somoud said. The alliance added that: "We demand that they refrain from remaining silent, as they did following previous airstrikes, and publicly state a clear position on what happened--particularly given their repeated invocation of sovereignty as a pretext for prolonging the war that is devastating the people of Sudan." Somoud also called for an urgent, independent investigation into the airstrikes, measures to protect miners, emergency medical care and assistance for those affected, and guarantees against the recurrence of such attacks. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Powers Future Growth With 'Digital Ethiopia 2030' Vision, Says DPM Temesgen
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Powers Future Growth With 'Digital Ethiopia 2030' Vision, Says DPM Temesgen - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Powers Future Growth With 'Digital Ethiopia 2030' Vision, Says DPM Temesgen 12 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh announced that Ethiopia is centering its long-term national prosperity on technology through the launch of the Digital Ethiopia 2030 vision. The announcement came as Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh officially launched Ethiopia's 7th National Cybersecurity Month under the theme "Active Citizen; Secured Country!" Emphasizing that cybersecurity is inseparable from national security, he urged all Ethiopians to play an active role in safeguarding the country's digital future. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn In a statement posted on his X page, the DPM highlighted that the achievements of Digital Ethiopia 2025. The gains include expanded internet access, telecom liberalization, digital payment systems, and digitized public services, have established a solid foundation for the country's ongoing digital transformation, he noted. He commended the Information Network Security Administration (INSA) for its "unwavering, round-the-clock efforts" in safeguarding Ethiopia's cyberspace. "Cybersecurity is national security," DPM Temesgen wrote, emphasizing that protecting cyberspace is "about defending our digital sovereignty, safeguarding our citizens, and securing the future of our nation." Stressing that cybersecurity cannot be left solely to government institutions, he framed digital defense as a collective duty. "An active citizenry is the foundation of a secure nation," he said, adding, "together, we must protect our digital sovereignty, strengthen national security, and secure Ethiopia's digital future." ethiopia.title: Ethiopia, IMF Discuss Strengthening Economic Partnership and Reforms
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, IMF Discuss Strengthening Economic Partnership and Reforms - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, IMF Discuss Strengthening Economic Partnership and Reforms 12 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) Eyob Tekalign has held talks with Zeine Zeidane, Director of the African Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF), on strengthening macroeconomic stability and advancing sustainable and inclusive economic growth in Ethiopia. The bilateral meeting took place on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok, providing an opportunity to review Ethiopia's macroeconomic reform agenda and explore ways to further strengthen cooperation with the international financial institution. In its press release sent to ENA, NBE noted that the discussions focused on progress in implementing Ethiopia's economic reforms, recent economic developments and priorities for sustaining the reform momentum. The two sides also exchanged perspectives on strengthening macroeconomic stability and creating favorable conditions for sustainable and inclusive growth. The engagement underscores Ethiopia's continued dialogue with the IMF as the country advances its macroeconomic reform efforts and seeks to reinforce economic stability and long-term development prospects, it was learned.
